svg.text: Why Sunflowers Use the Golden Angle
Same growth rule, one seed at a time from the center; only the turning angle differs

g.text: Seeds fall into spokes, wasted gaps
No two seeds ever line up
A plant adds one seed at a time from a central growing point, rotating by a fixed angle each time. If that angle is
close to a simple fraction of a full turn (1/2, 1/3, 2/5…), seeds line up into radial spokes and waste space.
The golden angle’s continued fraction is all 1’s, the single hardest number to approximate with any fraction.
That is why it wins. A 2015 biophysical model also finds it minimizes the energy cost when the growth
pattern changes as the plant develops: mechanism, not mystical design (Okabe, Scientific Reports, 2015).
